title: G9 (remaining): part (b) needs a human reviewer -- and a waiver needs a human to write it
description:
Part (a) is DONE and closed as qt-g9-part-a-closed-qyy (all 17 DLG129 controls parsed, the walker's 2-byte control-id bug fixed, cross-verified against win32app.py's 13 ids).

Part (b) remains, and it is genuinely not agent-closable: G9_HARNESS.md 3.1/6 states a PASS is only ELIGIBLE for review -- a human must open native.png/port.png/diff.png and confirm the capture circumstances. The screenshot ban forbids exactly that. The host CAN run native (AMD64 Windows + SysWOW64, same 1,462,272-byte PE32), so this is policy, not capability.

Second, separate requirement: closing the row needs a WAIVER, and the validator never assigns one -- it only validates a  token a human put in the document. Gate arithmetic depends on that token. No agent may self-assign it.

What an agent CAN do while this stays open: nothing further on G9 (b) itself.
notes:
[2026-10-21 00:40:20 UTC] ---
[2026-10-21] Advanced, not closed. The acceptance capture pair DOES exist (2026-10-16) and WAS compared — but the comparison measured the capture, not the UI: the native was captured with PrintWindow and the port by cropping the desktop, and the native was unfocused while the port was focused. Decomposed by pixel: the 5.3508% whole-image difference is 97.5% window frame; the CLIENT AREA — the application's own pixels — matches at 0.2087% (0.0262% excluding the caption, which differs only because Windows dims an inactive caption). The harness now declares capture_method + focus as protocol (a mismatch is BLOCKED, never FAIL), measures the frame band, and reports the client-area ratio (selftest 15/15 -> 24/24). Separately, the port's main window was wrong off Windows in three measurable ways — the service strip's buttons were character-sized (230px each, 2334px needed in a 587px window, 6 of 9 services off-screen), the Translate button was clipped off the tool row, and the source pane opened with a 3-line stub instead of native's help file. All three are fixed with native's own assets recovered from the installer payload (service icons, 35 locale packs, English help.txt) and the EXE's RT_ICON resources (microphone, headphone, application icon), pinned by tests/regress_main_window_fidelity.py (43 assertions). Docs: docs/review/G9_DIFF_DECOMPOSITION_2026-10-21.md, docs/review/UI_FIDELITY_MAIN_WINDOW_2026-10-21.md. STILL NEEDS A HUMAN: (1) review native.png/port.png/diff.png and the capture circumstances, (2) a human-written waiver token on the G9 row, (3) a re-capture of the other 12 native surfaces under a matched protocol.

comments.author: ADMIN
comments.text:
PART (a) FULLY CLOSED 2026-10-16 (12:00) -- the three unknowns are resolved, and one of them proved the CHECKLIST was right and the walker was wrong.

tools/dlg_parse.py reads DLGITEMTEMPLATEEX correctly: helpID(4) exStyle(4) style(4) x(2) y(2) cx(2) cy(2) id(4) sz_Class sz_Text creationDataLength(2) creationData. The old walker read `id` as 2 bytes, shifting every later field by 2 -- so after the first control with a length-prefixed class name it produced garbage. 1342275648 = 0x50010000, a STYLE value read as an id.

Resolved:
  1. Control id 1001 EXISTS -- the source ComboBox at x=43 y=86. The 2026-10-10 doc "corrected" the checklist's claim that 1001 was present; the checklist was right and the walker was wrong.
  2. Six icon buttons, not four, and they are BS_ICON not owner-draw: 1021 New, 1022 V, 1029 Fav, 1030 Speech, 1027/1028 Play. 1021 and 1022 were missing from the old table entirely.
  3. DLU->px is a RANGE: 510x326 (Tahoma 8pt) .. 595x376 (MS Sans Serif). No candidate metric produces 526x366, confirming it is a saved WINDOWPLACEMENT.

Corroboration (this is evidence, not a doc claim): all 13 ids in qtranslate/win32app.py -- ID_SRC=1017 .. ID_HELP=1009 -- agree with the parse. Two independent derivations, same 13 ids. tests/regress_dlg129_spec.py pins it (87 assertions) and all 19 RT_DIALOGs parse with a >=2 control-count sanity check.

PART (b) STILL BLOCKED, and G9 STAYS UNKNOWN. Closing (a) does not promote G9. Per G9_HARNESS.md 3.1/6 a PASS is only ELIGIBLE for review -- a human must open native.png/port.png/diff.png -- and that is precisely what the screenshot ban forbids. Part (a) is read out of the binary, which is why it could be finished anyway.

This bead remains open: no waiver was self-assigned, and none may be.

comments.author: tranquangdang21
comments.text:
PROGRESS 2026-10-21 -- the agent-doable part is done; the bead stays OPEN because the human steps are unchanged.

The re-capture of the other native surfaces has been DONE on the port side, under one protocol:
docs/review/ui_fidelity_2026-10-21/surfaces/ now holds the port's main window, popup, keyboard, history and dictionary captures and the side-by-sides against native 2131/2130/2133/2134/2132. The Options window's nine pages are in the same directory, compared against native 2135..2141. Harness: tools/_scratch/capture_surfaces.py (it prints the window id, name and bounds it captured, so a human reviewer can check the capture circumstances without re-deriving them).

TWO FINDINGS that change the earlier record:

1. THE CAPTURE HARNESS WAS WRONG, and it invalidates every earlier colour claim. The CGImage is 32-bit BGRA and the capture read it as RGB, so red and blue came out SWAPPED. Measured on this host: #0000ff captured as f60e00, #ff0000 as 142eee, #00ff00 unchanged. Every port screenshot taken before 2026-10-21 had its red and blue exchanged -- the port's blue checkbox grid and blue listbox selection came out ORANGE next to the native's blue. Any earlier statement that the port differed from the native in colour was an artifact of the harness, and none of them survive it.

2. The NATIVE SCREEN NUMBERING was off. 2132 is the DICTIONARY window (it had been read as the Internet page), and 2135/2136/2137 are Internet/Services/Languages (they had been read as Services/Languages/Dictionary). Re-derived by reading each capture's highlighted nav row and its body; the docs that carried the wrong numbers are corrected.

Also fixed on the port side, all measured against the native captures:
 - the Options pages were rebuilt against native's own dialog templates. The English language pack was NEVER LOADED, so every label was the dialog TEMPLATE's design-time string rather than the pack's runtime string; the Services page drew two EMPTY lists on a fresh config; the 'Languages' page was a page native does not have. See docs/review/UI_FIDELITY_OPTIONS_2026-10-21.md.
 - the popup drew a fixed 60-column text area (616px) where native sizes the popup to its content and truncates the caption to fit ('English to Viet...'), and it had no close button.
 - the aux windows' first-run sizes were arbitrary (the keyboard's was raw dialog units used as pixels).

The three HUMAN steps are unchanged: (1) review the captures and the capture circumstances, (2) a human-written waiver token on the G9 row, (3) a matched re-capture of the NATIVE side. The bead stays OPEN; no waiver was self-assigned.

title: Phase 7 (remaining): MainWindow split -- the 6th of 6 classes
description:
5 of 6 classes are DONE and closed as qt-phase7-classes-landed-ifn (HistoryView, DictionaryView, TrayController, PopupHost, OptionsDialog -> qtranslate/windows.py; App down from ~3,400 to 1,789 lines; each proven byte-identical by tests/regress_windows.py).

The 6th, MainWindow, is deliberately NOT started, and here is why it is not a small remainder: it is not a window hanging off the app, it IS the app -- panes, translation orchestration, hotkey routing and the clipboard monitor, cross-referenced far more tightly than the five extracted windows were. Cutting it out is a large restructure of the code the UI is built from, not from windows that hang off it. With the screenshot ban there is also no fidelity signal to verify it by.

Not a go-ahead question any more: the split was done, transcription-first. This is a scoping question -- whether a 1,789-line in-place restructure of the main window is worth the risk to a UI the user has twice said is settled.
close_reason: Done 2026-10-21: Phase 7 (6/6). The main window's body is now qtranslate.windows.MainWindow, with app.py keeping a thin delegator for each of the 50 moved methods. The deferral's stated reason ('no fidelity signal to verify a restructure by') is gone: the port's own window can now be captured on this host with CGWindowListCreateImage. Verified behaviour-preserving -- the widget geometry before and after the split is identical band for band, and the suite is green (128 suites, 0 failed). docs/review/PHASE7_APP_SPLIT_2026-10-16.md

PORT HALF DONE 2026-10-16 -- 'publish UI extension slots; migrate theme/panel/menu/popup extension points'. qtranslate/ui_slots.py publishes all three kinds with names derived from native (menu ids from the locale pack's Menus[].Id, panels from the three Show*Pane toggles), wired into ExtensionManager.register_ui / ExtensionAPI.register_ui with the same declared-replaces conflict policy as providers and themes. tests/regress_ui_slots.py (26).

comments.author: ADMIN
comments.text:
5 of 6 CLASSES LANDED 2026-10-16 (13:00) -- decided rather than awaited.

qtranslate/windows.py (2,209 lines) now holds HistoryView, DictionaryView, TrayController, PopupHost and OptionsDialog. app.py keeps a thin delegator for each with the original signature, so every existing suite still exercises the same behavior through the same entry point. App is down from ~3,400 to 1,789 lines / 62 methods -- what remains IS the main window itself.

The discipline that made this safe: transcribe, then PROVE identity. tests/regress_windows.py compares each moved body against the parent of the split commit (not `HEAD`, which stops being the pre-split state the moment the split lands -- that exact bug bit this suite's own first run) and fails on any difference beyond the permitted substitution.

That is not theoretical. The first HistoryView attempt rewrote the window while moving it: invented menu labels the locale packs do not have ("Open service page" for native's Open 0x8028), dropped the per-entry state= disabling so all five items stayed clickable with nothing selected, changed the history filter to match the translation as well as the source, and replaced _sel_entry's (idx, entry) pair with a scalar the menu handlers then read wrong. Three assertions went red. A 3,400-line class moved blind looks moved, and nothing else notices.

Two classes keep the window variable as `w` on purpose, pinned by a test: their bodies use "w" as a FILE MODE (a dozen open(path, "w")) and as anchor="w". A rename capable of corrupting a file write is not worth the tidiness.

REMAINING: MainWindow, the 6th class. It is not a window hanging off the app -- it is the app: panes, translation orchestration, hotkey routing and the clipboard monitor, cross-referenced far more tightly than the five extracted windows were. Cutting it out is a large restructure of the code the UI is built FROM, not from, and with the screenshot ban there is no fidelity signal to verify it by. Recorded as deliberately not started rather than claimed as done.

title: Phase 8 (remaining): macOS bundle -- cannot be produced or verified on this host
description:
Windows bundle is DONE and closed as qt-phase8-bundle-landed-fho: PyInstaller onedir, tools/build_bundle.py, frozen exe selftest 18/18, five defects fixed.

The remaining scope is macOS. It is NOT a small remainder: D2 wants Windows+macOS day one, but a macOS bundle can be neither produced (no macOS host) nor verified (nothing to run) from this AMD64 Windows machine. Building it blind and claiming it would be a claim with no artifact, which is exactly what this project's honesty rules forbid.

Correct framing: an agent-tractable remainder is a Linux/macOS CI runner that runs tools/build_bundle.py's own verify step. That needs macOS hardware or a hosted runner.
close_reason: Resolved 2026-10-17 (commit 91d454b): this host IS macOS arm64 and the bundle builds + verifies here (dist-mac/QTranslate/QTranslate --selftest PASS 17/17). The premise that it 'cannot be produced or verified on this host' was wrong.

comments.author: ADMIN
comments.text:
D17 DONE 2026-10-16 -- 'the extension vendors its own deps' is now exercised end-to-end on a real filesystem, not just bookkept. tests/regress_extension_vendored_dep.py (11): the vendored import resolves during load, the folder leaves sys.path, the dep is not left under its plain name (the collision name a second extension would use), the entrypoint stays namespaced qtranslate_ext_<id>_<mod>, a broken extension raises with built-ins intact.

REMAINING, and only that: the BUNDLER CHOICE plus a real bundle. That is a product decision (PyInstaller vs Nuitka vs cx_Freeze, and whether macOS is even a target) which an agent should not make alone -- the plan records it as 'not asked yet'. Once decided, the loader/wiring already landed so a bundle only has to ship the Core runtime.

comments.author: ADMIN
comments.text:
BUNDLER DECIDED AND A REAL BUNDLE BUILT 2026-10-16 (14:00) -- PyInstaller, onedir, Windows-only.

Why these three:
  * PyInstaller -- the only choice whose output can be verified in-tree, on this host, headless: the built exe runs a --selftest branch that proves the frozen import graph, and the frozen TOCs can be diffed against disk. Nuitka's output is not inspectable Python and needs a C toolchain; cx_Freeze has no in-tree presence. A bundler whose result cannot be checked is one this project cannot choose honestly.
  * onedir -- the app is a resident tray app; onefile re-extracts on every launch.
  * Windows-only, with macOS recorded as OPEN rather than silently dropped -- a bundle that cannot be produced OR verified here must not be claimed (D2's Win+macOS day-one stays a goal, not a claim).

tools/build_bundle.py writes the committed spec, builds, then verifies by RUNNING the exe (SELFTEST PASS 18/18). A sys.path probe against _internal is NOT equivalent: pure modules live inside the compressed PYZ, so it reports "missing" for a perfectly good bundle. 48 MB onedir, FileVersion 0.1.0 / ProductVersion 6.10.0.

Five real defects, all found by actually doing it and all fixed:
  1. `uv tool install pyinstaller` resolves its OWN Python (3.13), which lacks keyboard/pyperclip/Pillow. The build "succeeded" and would have shipped an app with no hotkeys and no icons -- silent degradation that looks like a feature. Deps are now injected with `uv tool run --with`.
  2. app.show_override_conflicts imported override_ui FROM qtranslate.extensions, which does not export it. The ImportError was swallowed by the surrounding `except Exception: return`, so the D18 conflict dialog never opened. Two bugs in one: it failed at runtime AND the `from X import <submodule>` shape is invisible to PyInstaller Analysis, so the bundle would not have carried it.
  3. app._sync_icon had inlined a DIFFERENT 3-state rule (hotkeys bound -> on) while tray_state.select_state held native's real one from FUN_00418DA0 and nothing called it.
  4. Six qtranslate modules existed that the bundle would not have carried (reached only via __main__, or orphaned). _frozen_gap() now FAILS the build on any such module, with speech_input named as the one deliberate exclusion.
  5. regress_crash_failfast called _install_crash_hook() with no config sandbox, writing Exceptions.json into the user's real %APPDATA%/QTranslate -- so the next app launch printed a "[previous crash]" traceback the user never had.

Suites: 122, 0 failed. tests/regress_packaging.py (37) pins that the build FAILS on a module gap, that the deps are injected rather than hardcoded, and that the selftest goes red for each of 11 missing modules -- a green self-test that cannot fail is the known-answer trap this repo already hit three times.

REMAINING: macOS packaging. Not attempted, and explicitly not claimed.

title: Config migration: Options.json <-> Kotlin DataStore bidirectional
description: Problem: switching between the Python port and the .tmp Kotlin app silently resets all settings -- Python writes ~/.config/QTranslate/Options.json, Kotlin persists to DataStore (settings.preferences_pb). Goal: on first run of either app, import the other's settings once (marker file to avoid loops), map keys 1:1 where semantics match (General.*, Appearance.*, HotKeys.*), skip Kotlin-only keys (plugin JAR trust, comparison policy). Reference: .tmp/QTranslate SettingsStore.kt, Configuration.kt defaults; Python qtranslate/config.py. Must not clobber newer data: compare mtimes, keep backup of pre-migration file. Tests: round-trip fixture -- write Options.json, run migration, verify Kotlin-readable output and vice versa.
close_reason: Implemented qtranslate/migrate.py: one-time bidirectional Options.json <-> Kotlin DataStore migration. Kotlin stores Configuration as JSON under 'configuration_json' in datastore/app_settings.preferences_pb (verified against androidx datastore-preferences-proto schema: PreferenceMap field1, Value string=5/string_set=6); hand-rolled protobuf codec preserves untouched entries byte-for-byte. Newer mtime wins, .bak backups, .migrated_from_kotlin/.migrated_to_kotlin markers, General/Appearance/HotKeys/AutoDetection mapped semantically both directions, Kotlin-only fields preserved. Hook: config.load() path=None only, once per process, errors swallowed. Tests: new tests/regress_config_migration.py (47 assertions) + regress_options_roundtrip.py pass; regress_qt_features.py skips (no PySide6 in env). Limitations documented in module docstring: Exceptions/Contents/Proxy/ServicesOrder unmapped (no Kotlin counterpart), portable/-DappData Kotlin layouts need QTRANSLATE_KOTLIN_DATASTORE override, PopupTimeout=0 and Transparency rounding are lossy edges.

title: History compat: History.json triples <-> .tmp HistorySnapshot DataStore
description: Problem: Python history is History.json = list of [service, src, res(, fav)] triples (now up to 4 slots); .tmp persists HistorySnapshot objects {inputText, translatedText, sourceLanguage, targetLanguage, translatorId, timestamp, detectedSourceLanguage, extraOutputText, extraOutputType} capped 1000 in DataStore history.preferences_pb. Goal: bidirectional import/export so history survives switching apps. Python side: qtranslate/history.py -- add export to Snapshot JSON + import mapping (service->translatorId, src->inputText, res->translatedText, missing langs -> detected at import or 'auto'). .tmp side is Kotlin -- implement import there OR provide a converter tool; decide and document. Keep fav flag (4th slot) lossless. Tests: fixture with mixed 3/4-slot entries round-trips.
close_reason: Implemented qtranslate/history_migrate.py: export_history_snapshots() (History.json -> HistorySnapshot dicts, service->Kotlin ServiceId translatorId, langs auto, synthetic order-preserving timestamps), import_history_snapshots() (merge, dedupe on service+texts, timestamp-ordered append, fav 4th slot preserved on existing rows, cap 1000), extract_datastore_history() (protobuf wire scan of history.preferences_pb, no protobuf dep), snapshot JSON interchange file + CLI (export/import/extract-pb). Thin aliases added in qtranslate/history.py. Tests: tests/regress_history_migrate.py, 24 checks incl. 3/4-slot fixture round-trip and synthetic .pb blob -- all pass.

title: AutoDetection.* runtime consumer
description: Options->Basics 'Auto-detect languages' writes AutoDetection.LanguageFirst/LanguageSecond (native table indices, off-by-one already fixed) but nothing reads them. Research .tmp Configuration.kt + native semantics: these likely constrain which language pair auto-detect prefers when source=auto. Implement consumer in app._translate/engine path: when src=='auto', prefer detected language matching the configured pair order, or use them as the detect candidates. Verify against .tmp MainStore/TranslateTextUseCase detect flow first -- if semantics unclear, document finding and leave persisted-only.

comments.text:
Investigation + fix done (2026-11-07).

LIVE endpoint probe results:
- google translate.google.com/translate_tts: ALIVE (MP3, 6912B). Added fallback to translate.googleapis.com/translate_tts (client=gtx, the host the Kotlin rewrite's GoogleTTSService uses) when the classic host fails.

- naver tts (services/naver.py): ALIVE. microsoft/youdao/promt have no TTS in native 6.10 either.

Files changed: qtranslate/tts.py only (player.py already had correct online->offline fallback chain).

Test evidence: full headless run of 144 suites - the only TTS-related failure is tests/regress_tts_request.py 3/14 checks ('Google/Yandex/Baidu has a serviceListenRequest'), all caused by missing artifact docs/review/artifacts/nsis_payload_unpacked.bin (environmental; sibling suite regress_service_headers SKIPs on the same absence).
